questions.question: Which two signs need to be interchanged to make the following equation correct? 45 ÷ 15 × 5 + 15 −11 = 39
questions.questionHtml:
Which two signs need to be interchanged to make the following equation correct?

45 ÷ 15 × 5 + 15 −11 = 39
questions.solution:
BODMAS Rule: 

Option 1) - and +

Given Equation: 45 ÷ 15 × 5 + 15 −11 = 39

After interchanging sign we get: 

⇒ 45 ÷ 15 × 5 - 15 + 11 = 39

⇒ 3 × 5 - 15 + 11 = 39

⇒ 15 - 15 + 11 = 39

⇒ 26 - 15 = 39

⇒ 11 ≠ 39

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Option 2) - and ×

Given Equation: 45 ÷ 15 × 5 + 15 −11 = 39

After interchanging sign we get: 

⇒ 45 ÷ 15 - 5 + 15 × 11 = 39 

⇒ 3 - 5 + 15 × 11 = 39

⇒ 3 - 5 + 165 = 39

⇒ 168 - 5 = 39

⇒ 163 ≠ 39

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Option 3) + and ×

Given Equation: 45 ÷ 15 × 5 + 15 −11 = 39

After interchanging sign we get: 

⇒ 45 ÷ 15 + 5 × 15 −11 = 39

⇒ 3 + 5 × 15 - 11 = 39

⇒ 3 + 75 - 11 = 39

⇒ 78 - 11 = 39

⇒ 67 ≠ 39

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Option 4) ÷ and +

Given Equation: 45 ÷ 15 × 5 + 15 −11 = 39

After interchanging sign we get: 

⇒ 45 + 15 × 5 ÷ 15 −11 = 39

⇒ 45 + 15 × 0.33 - 11 = 39

⇒ 45 + 5 - 11 = 39

⇒ 50 - 11 = 39

⇒ 39 = 39

⇒ LHS = RHS

Hence, the correct answer is "÷ and +".

  • ​Seaweeds are abundant along the Tamil Nadu and Gujarat coasts and around Lakshadweep and Andaman & Nicobar Islands.

questions.question: Carbon monoxide contains approximately ______ of oxygen for each 1.00 g of carbon.
questions.questionHtml: Carbon monoxide contains approximately ______ of oxygen for each 1.00 g of carbon.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1.33 g.

Key Points

  • Every sample of carbon monoxide contains 16.0 g of oxygen for every 12.0 g of carbon.
  • This is a mass ratio of oxygen to carbon of 1.33 to 1.
  • In carbon dioxide, there is exactly twice as much oxygen present as there is in carbon monoxide.
  • This illustrates the law of multiple proportions:
    • whenever the same two elements form more than one compound, the different masses of one element that combine with the same mass of the other element are in the ratio of small whole numbers.
  • In carbon monoxide, there is 1.333g oxygen for every 1g carbon.
  • In carbon dioxide, there is 2.666g oxygen for every gram of carbon.
  • So the ratio of oxygen in the two compounds is 1:2, a small whole-number ratio.​

Important Points

  • Carbon monoxide is a deadly gas. 
  • It is formed from the incomplete combustion of some carbon-containing materials (such as wood and gasoline).
  • It will attach to haemoglobin in the red blood cells and block the binding of oxygen to those cells.
  • If oxygen does not bind, it cannot be carried to the cells of the body where it is needed, and death can occur.
  • Carbon dioxide, on the other hand, is not toxic like carbon monoxide is.
  • However, it can displace oxygen in systems since it is heavier.
  • Carbon dioxide fire extinguishers cut off the flow of oxygen in a fire, putting out the fire.

questions.question: Organisms belonging to the phylum ______ are also called ‘flatworms’.
questions.questionHtml: Organisms belonging to the phylum ______ are also called ‘flatworms’.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Platyhelminthes.

Key Points

  • Animals belonging to the phylum Platyhelminthes are also called flatworms due to their dorsoventrally flattened bodies.
  • Examples are a liver fluke, tapeworm, etc.
  • They are found as endoparasites in human beings.
  • About 80 percent of all flatworms are parasitic—i.e., living on or in another organism and securing nourishment from it.
  • They are bilaterally symmetrical (i.e., the right and left sides are similar) and lack specialized respiratory, skeletal, and circulatory systems.
  • The body cavity (coelom) is absent.
  • The body is not segmented; spongy connective tissue (mesenchyme) constitutes the so-called parenchyma and fills the space between organs.
  • Flatworms are generally hermaphroditic—functional reproductive organs of both sexes occurring in one individual. 

Additional Information

    • They are radially symmetrical and diploblastic.
  • Porifera​
    • ​These are pore-bearing multicellular animals.
    • The body has no organs.
    • They exhibit holozoic nutrition.
    • The body is radially symmetrical.
    • They can regenerate their lost parts.
  • Cnidaria
    • ​Mostly marine animals, the cnidarians include the corals, hydras, and jellyfish.
    • Radial symmetry.
    • Diploblastic animals.
    • Tissue level of organization.
    • Presence of cnidoblasts with stinging nematocysts on the tentacles.

Additional Information

  • Taxes are of two types;
  • Direct taxes:
    • They are paid in entirety by a taxpayer directly to the government.
    • The tax where the liability, as well as the burden to pay it, resides on the same individual.
    • Direct taxes include tax varieties such as income tax, corporate tax, wealth tax, gift tax, expenditure tax etc.​
    • Types of direct tax include :
      • Income Tax: Levied on and paid by the same person according to tax brackets as defined by the income tax department.

      • Wealth Tax: Levied on the value of the property that a person holds.
      • Estate Duty: Paid by an individual in case of inheritance.
      • Gift Tax: An individual receiving the taxable gift pays tax to the government.
      • Fringe Benefits Tax: Paid by an employer that provides fringe benefits to employees, and is collected by the state government.
  • Indirect tax:
  • Taxes, where the liability to pay the tax, lies on a person who then shifts the tax burden to another individual.
  • Types of indirect taxes are :
    • Excise Duty: Payable by the manufacturer who shifts the tax burden to retailers and wholesalers.

questions.question: Irrespective of the source, pure water contains ______ of oxygen by mass.
questions.questionHtml: Irrespective of the source, pure water contains ______ of oxygen by mass.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 88.89%.

 Key Points

  • A sample of pure water, whatever the source always contains 88.89% by mass of oxygen and 11.1%by mass of hydrogen.
  • This is according to the law of constant composition.
    • Water (H₂O) molecule consists of two hydrogen atoms of relative mass 1 and one oxygen atom of relative mass 16.
    • Therefore, the ratio in which 2 atoms of hydrogen and one atom of oxygen are combined is 1: 8.
  • It will always be the same irrespective of the source of water.
  • The total amount of percentage is 100, therefore they are divided in a constant ratio.
  • As 2 atoms of hydrogen and one atom of oxygen are divided in a ratio of 1:8.
  • Therefore the mass of Oxygen in percentage terms in the compound is 88.89%.

 Important Points

  • The chemical formula of water is H2O.
  • Water contains two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.
  • The molar mass of water, = 2×atomic mass of hydrogen + 1×atomic mass of oxygen.
  • Therefore, the molar mass of water= 2×1+16=18g.
  • Mass of oxygen in water: 16 g.
  • Mass of hydrogen in water: 2 g.
  • The formula for calculating the percent composition of any element in a given compound is:
    • The mass percent of element = (Mass of that element in the compound/ Molar mass of compound)×100.
    • So, mass % of hydrogen in H2O = (mass of hydrogen in H2O/Molar mass of H2O)×100
    • = (2/18)×100
    •  =11.1%.
    • Now, mass % of oxygen in H2O = (Mass of oxygen in H2O/Molar mass of H2O)×100

                  =(16/18)×100

                   =88.8%.

 Additional Information

  • Law of constant composition
    • In a given compound, the elements always combine in the same proportion as each other.
    • This implies that any pure sample of a compound, no matter the source, will always consist of the same elements present in the same ratio by mass.
    • For example, pure water always contains hydrogen and oxygen in a fixed mass ratio.

questions.question: ______ is an environmental policy under which producers are given a significant responsibility - financial and/or physical - for the treatment or disposal of products that are no longer useful to the consumer.
questions.questionHtml: ______ is an environmental policy under which producers are given a significant responsibility - financial and/or physical - for the treatment or disposal of products that are no longer useful to the consumer.
questions.solution:
Concept:

Environmental policy:

  • It is a kind of measure or unit that is taken by a different kind of organization like government and private regarding a different kind of effect of human activities on the environment.
  • This is majorly created for the prevention of human-made effects on the ecosystem.
  • Different kinds of environmental policies are ecosystem management, waste management, natural resources protection, and biodiversity conservation.

Explanation:

Extended Producer Responsibility:

  • This policy's concept was first introduced by the Swedish Ministry of Environment in 1990.
  • Today's world is facing an increasing amount of waste and its effect on the environment.
  • Different governments around the world are trying to control this problem with the post-consumer phase by environmental policy.
  • The correct answer is Extended Producer Responsibility.
  • EPR refers to an environmental policy that sees producers responsible for the safe disposal of their products.
  • It is the responsibility, that the waste generated during the production processes should be taken care of in a proper way, from an environmental and resource-saving point of view.
  • Before the manufacturing of a product is commenced it should be known how the waste, which is a result of the production process, should be treated, as well as how the product should be taken care of when discarded.
  • The ultimate goal of EPR is sustainable development through environmentally responsible product development and product recovery.
  • Its main objective is to divert and reduce waste.
  • Here producers of a product take full responsibility for their products' whole lifecycle including recycling, reuse, final disposal, and packaging.

Thus, extended producer responsibility is an environmental policy under which producers are given a significant responsibility - financial and/or physical - for the treatment or disposal of products that are no longer useful to the consumer.

questions.question: 20 men can finish a work in 30 days. They started working, but 4 men left the work after 10 days. In how many days would the work be completed?
questions.questionHtml: 20 men can finish a work in 30 days. They started working, but 4 men left the work after 10 days. In how many days would the work be completed?
questions.solution:
Total work days = 20 × 30 = 600 man-days

Total work done in 10 days = 20 × 10 = 200 man-days

Total work remaining = 600 - 200 = 400 man-days

Total time needed to complete the remaining work = 400 ÷ 16 = 25

Total time needed to complete the whole work = 25 + 10 = 35 days

questions.question: Find the greatest 3-digit number which, when divided by 3, 4, 5 and 8, leaves remainder 2 in each case.
questions.questionHtml: Find the greatest 3-digit number which, when divided by 3, 4, 5 and 8, leaves remainder 2 in each case.
questions.solution:
Concept:

We need to find a common multiple for a set of numbers i.e., LCM of the numbers. This is followed by division with the largest three-digit number and addition of the remainder. 

Calculations:

LCM of 3, 4, 5, and  8 = 120

Greatest three-digit number = 999

Largest three-digit number that is exactly divisible by 120 = 960 (120 × 8 = 960)

Greatest three-digit number that would leave remainder 2 when divided by 120 = 960 + 2 = 962

∴ The largest three-digit number that would leave remainder 2 when divided by 3, 4, 5, and 8 is 962.

questions.question: The average of twelve numbers is 42. The average of the last five numbers is 40, and that of the first four numbers is 44. The sixth number is 6 less than the fifth number and 5 less than the seventh number. The average of the sixth and seventh numbers is:
questions.questionHtml: The average of twelve numbers is 42. The average of the last five numbers is 40, and that of the first four numbers is 44. The sixth number is 6 less than the fifth number and 5 less than the seventh number. The average of the sixth and seventh numbers is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Net deviation of first 4 numbers = 4 × (44 − 42) = +8

Net deviation of last 5 numbers = 5 × (40 − 42) = −10

Sum of 5th, 6th, and 7th numbers = (3 × 42) − (8 − 10) = 126 + 2 = 128

Let 6th number be x, then (x + 6) + x + (x + 5) = 128 ⇒ 3x = 117 ⇒ x = 39

Average of 6th (39) and 7th (44) = (39 + 44) ÷ 2 = 41.5

∴ The correct option is D.

Alternate Method

Given:

Average of 12 numbers = 42

Average of first 4 numbers = 44

Average of last 5 numbers = 40

6th number is 6 less than 5th and 5 less than 7th.

Formula Used:

Sum = Average × Number of observations

Calculations:

⇒ Total sum of 12 numbers = 12 × 42 = 504

⇒ Sum of first 4 numbers = 4 × 44 = 176

⇒ Sum of last 5 numbers = 5 × 40 = 200

⇒ Sum of 5th, 6th, and 7th numbers = 504 − (176 + 200) = 504 − 376 = 128

⇒ Let 6th number = x

⇒ 5th number = x + 6

⇒ 7th number = x + 5

⇒ (x + 6) + x + (x + 5) = 128

⇒ 3x + 11 = 128 ⇒ 3x = 117 ⇒ x = 39

⇒ 6th number = 39, 7th number = 39 + 5 = 44

⇒ Average of 6th and 7th numbers = (39 + 44) ÷ 2 = 83 ÷ 2 = 41.5

∴ The correct option is D.

Additional Information

Average Concept

Average = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations). It represents the central value of a data set.

Deviation Method

The sum of deviations of all observations from the actual mean is always zero. This property helps in finding missing values quickly.

Weighted Average

When two or more groups are combined, the new average A = (n1a1 + n2a2) ÷ (n1 + n2), where n is the count and a is the individual group average.

The divisibility test for 6 states that for a number to be divisible by 6, it should be divisible by 2 and 3.

The number k53206k would be divisible by 2 if k is an even number i.e., 2, 4, 6, or 8.

questions.questionHtml:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. They always shared machinery and goods as needed without a hitch.

B. Then they had the first serious quarrel in 40 years of farming side by side.

C. And unfortunately, the long collaboration fell apart.

D. Two brothers lived on adjoining farms in a small village.
questions.solution: Statement D is the opening line it begins by giving the background of the story. Statement A is the second sentence of the passage as it continues the story of the two brothers who always shared machinery and goods as needed without a hitch. Statement B is the third sentence of the passage as it begins with "then" which marks a moment in time. In the given sentence, we are told about the first time the brothers had a quarrel. Statement C is the last sentence as it begins with the conjunction "and" which links the previous statement to this one.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2.

Key Points

  • The given sentence is in the past tense.
  • So we need to use the past tense form of the verb "get" which is "got"
  • There are two clauses in the sentence which are linked by a conjunction.
  • The use of the conjunction "but" is incorrect here.
  • There are two events happening at the same time or very close to each other.
  • We need to use the subordinate conjunction "when"
  • The subordinate conjunction when is used to denote time in a sentence,
  • When is used to talk about events that took place in the past.
  • In the given sentence, the speaker wants to say they had hardly entered the train when the train started moving.

The correct sentence is: Hardly had we got in when the train started.

Hence, the correct sentence is option 2.
